comments.body:
Precondition met 2026-11-11 17:30 PST: Jira version `rebar-fixver-probe` (id 10035) created in REB (project id 16904) by the configured Jira identity, via Jira REST `POST /rest/api/3/version`, from coordinator session 3d705fec. `GET /rest/api/3/project/REB/versions` now returns ["rebar-fixver-probe"].

Screen check (read-only, 17:30 PST): `GET /rest/api/3/issue/REB-7117/editmeta` still has no `fixVersions` field after the version exists. So the "one version is enough" reading of JRA-59796 does not hold for REB on its own; whether the outbound write is still accepted (Atlassian's edit endpoint documents that it does not check screen configuration) is what this ticket's rebar→Jira step settles. If Jira rejects the write, record status and body; adding Fix versions to REB's edit screen is a Jira-admin screen-scheme change.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

plucky-jetblack-parrot checked the fix-version sync live on the production bridge through a rebar probe ticket, but REB has no Jira versions and the bridge never creates one (ADR 0124 decision 8), so only the missing-version path could run live. Two live checks still need a version that exists in REB:
- Jira to rebar: a Fix version set on a bound REB issue appears in the bound rebar ticket's `releases` after the next bridge run.
- rebar to Jira: a release set in rebar that names an existing REB version is written to the issue's Fix versions with the per-item `update` add verb.
This check also settles ADR 0124's open question: REB's edit metadata omits Fix versions (it did on 2026-11-11 for all 4 issue types), while Jira Cloud documents that `PUT /issue` does not check screen configuration and that Fix versions is not editable in a project with no versions. Record which holds once a version exists.

## Approach

1. Precondition: a version exists in REB, created by a person (not the bridge). Read it with `GET /rest/api/3/project/REB/versions`.
2. Create two clearly labelled probe tickets through rebar with `bridge_project=REB`, linked `relates_to` this ticket (not children): probe A for rebar to Jira and probe B for Jira to rebar, since a release that arrived from Jira is never pushed back (bug a06c intent rule). Read each REB key from `.bridge_state/bindings.json` on the tickets branch after the first bridge run.
3. rebar to Jira: add the existing version's name as a release in rebar; after the first bridge run started after that write, `GET /rest/api/3/issue/<KEY>?fields=fixVersions` lists it. If Jira rejects the write, record the status and body from the run log (`update_one: fix version add failed`).
4. Jira to rebar: set the version on probe B's issue in Jira (Jira REST `PUT /rest/api/3/issue/<KEY>` with `update.fixVersions` add, or acli, using the configured identity); after the next run `rebar show` lists it in `releases`.
5. Steady state: the next run writes no event on the probe and no Fix versions change.
6. Record run ids and PST times in a comment; close the probe as obsolete.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [non-codebase] A release naming an existing REB version is written to the bound issue's Fix versions by the production bridge.
  provenance: environment=production reconcile-bridge.yml on main and Jira Cloud REB; principal=bridge account; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — run id and REST excerpt
- [ ] [non-codebase] A Fix version set in Jira appears in the bound rebar ticket's `releases` after the next run.
  provenance: environment=production bridge; principal=bridge account; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — run id and `rebar show` excerpt
- [ ] [non-codebase] The following run writes nothing for either direction.
  provenance: environment=production bridge; principal=bridge account; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — run id and tracker event count
- [ ] A comment records whether the write needed Fix versions on REB's edit screen (ADR 0124 screen question).
compiled_state.title: Live-check fix-version sync with a real REB version (Jira to rebar, and a rebar release written to Jira)
